summary: Synchronized retry wave from orchestrated worker pool causing tenant 429 cascade
description:
Issue summary: Over a 3-hour window on 2026-03-12 the customer reported repeated 429 throttles for multiple services across their tenant following a scheduled workers rollout. Impact: several downstream ingestion pipelines stalled (PEAK ~600 rps reduced to 40 rps) and a burst of retries from their orchestrator amplified token exhaustion across routes. The customer observed the failures beginning immediately after their orchestrated worker fleet performed a simultaneous restart with identical retry configuration.

We believe this is a synchronized retry wave combined with per-tenant token accounting that allowed coordinated retries to exhaust the tenant window instead of smoothing across time. Customer-facing errors were HTTP 429 with X-RateLimit headers showing near-zero remaining tokens for the tenant window.

Customer notes: They run an internal orchestrator (K8s CronJob-based) that restarts 250 ephemeral workers in parallel during their daily backfill. Each worker uses the official SDK with an internal exponential backoff but no randomized jitter. The customer requested guidance and mitigation to avoid recurring tenant-wide throttles.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure an orchestrated fleet (200-300 workers) to process parallel tasks in prod-us-east.
2) Each worker reads from a queue and on transient 5xx or 429 retries with exponential backoff (base=200ms, cap=5s) but no jitter.
3) Trigger a coordinated restart so workers retry the same request batch at roughly the same time.
4) Observe tenant-level rate-limit headers and 429 spread across multiple API routes.
5) Verify spike in token consumption in metrics (tenant_token_usage, per-route accounting).
logs:
-- Customer-provided snippets: X-Request-Id: req_7a9f...; Response: 429 Too Many Requests; X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000; X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0; X-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-03-12T13:04:00Z
-- Proxy / gateway logs show repeated request bursts from 10.10.10.0/24 clustered timestamps (2026-03-12T12:59:54Z - 2026-03-12T13:01:12Z).
-- Internal rate-limiter metrics: tenant-window-consumption: stepped to 100% in <90s after restart.
-- Customer SDK logs: "Retry attempt 1 after 200ms" repeated across many hosts with identical timings.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by CS: confirmed patterns across tenant token accounting (not per-key). Confirmed customer had no jitter configured in their retry logic. Eng SRE (Marco) pulled rate-limiter metrics and trace samples. Observed distinct sawtooth pattern in token consumption matching worker restart time. Reviewed gateway logs (linked PR updates) and no anomalies on server-side scheduling. Hypothesis: synchronized retries create transient high-concurrency pulses that the tenant token bucket cannot absorb, causing immediate 429s.

What we've checked:
- Per-route vs per-tenant accounting: counting aggregated to tenant window during bursts.
- No server-side misconfiguration of refill rates.
- No scheduled maintenance or autoscale events at exact time.
- Customer-side orchestrator did a rolling restart with zero stagger.

Next steps: suggest immediate mitigations (client-side fixes) and consider adding tenant-side soft-queueing or short smoothing window as a platform mitigation for orchestration-driven waves. Priority for SRE to propose a short-term protection knob (rate limiter soft-shaper) and long-term documentation for jitter/backoff defaults in SDKs.

resolution_notes:
Workarounds provided: 1) Customer added random jitter to client retry logic (recommended uniform jitter up to 1000ms) and implemented staggered worker restart windows. 2) Redwood SRE applied a one-time +15% burst allowance for 30 minutes to absorb the first controlled restart. Outcome: Controlled test passed without tenant-wide 429 cascade.

Follow-ups:
- SRE to evaluate implementing short-term soft-shaper that smooths tenant token spikes (RFC due 2026-03-28).
- SDK team to publish a jittered retry pattern example and default snippet in the client repo (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/client/pull/1102).
- CS to send post-incident guidance to StellarDocs and update runbook.
root_cause: Coordinated retries from a large fleet without jitter/stagger produced transient token-window exhaustion at tenant level. No server-side bug found; behavior expected under current tenant token accounting.
